days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: tanişiş uçun iboralar, to be fe’li (am / is / are), sinf buyumlari va 1–20 sonlari bilan gapiriş hamda yoziş.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: ma’nosini bilgan sözni belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: “sinf xonasi” = classroom.
exercises.question: Which word means "sinf xonasi"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sonni inglizça söz bilan yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: 10 + 5 = 15 (fifteen), 9 + 9 = 18 (eighteen).
exercises.text: Ten and five is ___. Nine and nine is ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: salomlaşiş iborasini özbekçaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: Goodbye — xayr, körişgunça.
accepted: Xayr, ertaga körişamiz!
Xayr, ertaga körişgunça
Körişgunça, ertaga

exercises.instructionUz: Test: töğri grammatik variantni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Köplikdagi “these pencils” bilan are işlatiladi.
exercises.question: These pencils ___ mine.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 1-kun matnini eslab, fikrga baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Birinçi paragrafda bugun duşanba deyilgan.
exercises.statement: Samir writes about a Monday.
exercises.evidence: Today is Monday. I am very happy.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: audioyadagi ma’lumotni eslab, javobni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Öqituvçi: See you at eight o’clock.
exercises.question: What time do the students come back to class?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: raqamlarni ularning inglizça nomlari bilan birlaştiring.
exercises.explanationUz: 7 — seven, 12 — twelve, 15 — fifteen, 20 — twenty.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sözlardan ism haqidagi gapni tartiblab çiqaring.
exercises.explanationUz: Töğri gap: Her name is Gulnoza.

days.goalUz: Kundalik hayotda oilani taniştiriş: egalik ('s, my/your), have got / has got va odamni taşqi körinişi bilan tavsiflaş.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: testda qarindoşlik atamalarini ma’nosi bilan boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: brother — aka/uka, aunt — xola, parents — ota-ona, hair — soç.

exercises.instructionUz: Testda yoş ifodasini töğri variantdan tanlab oling.
exercises.explanationUz: Bibim 70 yoşda: “My grandmother is seventy years old.”
exercises.question: Your grandmother is 70. You say: “My grandmother ...”

exercises.instructionUz: Testda inkor şaklini töğri yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Inkor: has not got / hasn’t got.
exercises.text: My uncle ___ a car. He has a bike.

exercises.instructionUz: 2-kun matniga asoslanib, fikrga true / false / notgiven deb baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Ikkinçi paragrafda otaning kasbi aytilmagan — faqat “he is quiet, he has got a bike” deyilgan.
exercises.statement: Dilnoza’s father is a doctor.
exercises.evidence: Ota haqida faqat böyi, xarakteri va velosipedi aytilgan.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: audioda eşitgan ma’lumotni eslab, töğri javobni belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: Sardor: “My father is tall and he has got short black hair.”
exercises.question: What has Sardor’s father got?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: özbekça egalik ifodasini ingliz tiliga aylantiring.
exercises.explanationUz: ‘Otamning velosipedi’ = My father's bike.
accepted: This is my father's bike
This is the bike of my father
It is my father's bike

exercises.instructionUz: Testda söroq gapning töğri şaklini topib belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: Söroqda have egadan oldin çiqadi: Has your sister got long hair?
exercises.question: Which question is correct?
options: Has your sister got long hair?
Your sister has got long hair?
Has got your sister long hair?
Is your sister got long hair?

exercises.instructionUz: Testdagi böş joylarga sifat sözlarini qöying.
exercises.explanationUz: tall — baland böyli, young — yoş, tall uçun opposite — short.
exercises.text: My grandfather is not young, he is ___. My brother is not short, he is ___.

days.goalUz: Present Simple yordamida öz kunduzini sözlab beriş: uyanişdan uxlagunça, hafta kunlari va soatni aytiş.

sections.titleUz: Yangi sözlar: kunlik tartib va vaqt
Grammatika: Present Simple va vaqt prepozitsiyalari

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sözma-söz aytilgan vaqtni raqamli şaklga boğlang.
exercises.explanationUz: half past seven = 7:30, a quarter past eight = 8:15, a quarter to nine = 8:45.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: vaqt prepozitsiyalarini töğri qöying.
exercises.explanationUz: Soat — at, hafta kuni — on, kunduz qismi — in.
exercises.text: School starts ___ eight o’clock. We have an English lesson ___ Monday. I do my homework ___ the afternoon.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: uçinçi şaxs şakli qöllangan gapni toping.
exercises.explanationUz: My sister — uçinçi şaxs yagona: watches.
exercises.question: My sister ___ TV in the evening.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: otangiz haqidagi gapni sözlar bilan tuzib çiqing.
exercises.explanationUz: Töğri gap: My father gets up at half past five.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: audioyadagi ma’lumotga suyangan holda baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: “In the evening I do my homework and I play tennis with my sister.”
exercises.statement: Bekzod does his homework in the evening.
exercises.evidence: In the evening I do my homework and I play tennis with my sister.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: öqilgan matndan bir savolga javob toping.
exercises.explanationUz: “We have lunch at twelve o’clock at school.”
exercises.question: Where does Aziza have lunch?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: hafta kunlarining nomlarini inglizça yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Biz duşanbadan juma rigaça öqiymiz: Monday. Dam oliş kunlari — Saturday, Sunday.
exercises.text: We have lessons from ___ to Friday. The weekend days are ___ and ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: soat sörovi haqidagi özbekça gapni inglizçaga aylantiring.
exercises.explanationUz: uxlaşga bormoq = go to bed; “soat töqqizda” = at nine o’clock; “keçqurun” = in the evening.
accepted: He goes to bed at nine o’clock in the evening
He goes to bed at nine o'clock in the evening
He goes to bed at nine in the evening
He sleeps at nine o’clock in the evening
She goes to bed at nine o’clock in the evening

days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: uy-xona sözlari (house, kitchen, bedroom ...), “There is / There are” va in / on / under / next to predloglari bilan joyini aytiş.

sections.titleUz: Yangi sözlar: uy, xonalar va joy predloglari
Grammatika: There is / There are va joy predloglari

exercises.instructionUz: Test: ovqat pişiriladigan xonani inglizça belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: “oşxona” = kitchen.
exercises.question: Which word means "oşxona"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: böş joyga töğri predlogni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Yostiq karavot ustida — on (“ustida”).
exercises.question: The pillow is ___ the bed.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: töğri grammatik şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: “three lamps” köplik, şuning uçun There are.
exercises.question: ___ three lamps in the shop.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: böş joylarni töğri sözlar bilan töldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: Bitta deraza — is; “two doors” — are; “two doors” yozilişi "two".
exercises.text: There ___ one window in my room. There ___ two doors. Two and one is ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 4-kun öqiş matnini eslab, fikrga baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda oşxona vanna xonasi yonida deyilgan.
exercises.statement: The kitchen is next to the bathroom.
exercises.evidence: The kitchen is next to the bathroom.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 4-kun tinglaş matniga asoslanib baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Transkriptda oşxonada ovqat bor deyilgan, stullar soni esa 4 ta.
exercises.statement: There are four chairs in the kitchen.
exercises.evidence: This is the kitchen. There are four chairs and a big table in it.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sözlarni tartib bilan qöying.
exercises.explanationUz: Töğri gap: Is there a bathroom in your flat?
exercises.noteUz: Eslatma: sözlar orasiga "?" qöyiş şart emas.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni inglizçaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Mehmonxonada katta divan bor” = There is a big sofa in the living room.
accepted: There is a big sofa in the living room
There’s a big sofa in the living room
There is a big sofa in the living room.

days.titleUz: Ovqat va içimliklar: birozmi, yoki yöqmi?
days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: ovqat va içimlik sözlari, “some / any” hamda sanaladigan–sanalmaydigan ismlar, “I like cooking” kabi “like + -ing” gaplar.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: “çanqagan” sözining inglizçasini belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: thirsty — çanqagan; hungry — oç.
exercises.question: Which word means "çanqagan"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: böş joyga töğri sözni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Söroq gapda any işlatiladi.
exercises.question: Are there ___ bananas in the bag?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: qaysi gap töğri?
exercises.explanationUz: “water” sanalmaydigan, şuning uçun isn’t any.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: There aren’t any waters in the glass.
There isn’t any water in the glass.
There isn’t any waters in the glass.
There are any water in the glass.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: böş joylarni töldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: like’den keyin cooking; tasdiqda some; inkorda any.
exercises.text: My father enjoys ___ dinner. There is ___ bread on the table. There isn’t ___ tea in the cup.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 5-kun öqiş matnini eslab, baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda guruç, göşt va tuxum sotib olingan; sut esa xarid qilinmagan.
exercises.statement: The family buys rice and meat at the market.
exercises.evidence: We buy two kilos of rice, some meat and ten eggs.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 5-kun tinglaş matniga asoslanib baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Malika oç (hungry) ekanini aytadi; çanqaganligi esa NEÇA töğri neça notöğri ekanini audio aytmaydi — Not Given.
exercises.statement: Malika is thirsty at first.
exercises.evidence: Good morning! I am hungry. Is there any bread for breakfast?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sözlarni töğri tartibda qöying.
exercises.explanationUz: Töğri gap: I like eating apples with my sister.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni inglizçaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Oşxonada biroz non bor” = There is some bread in the kitchen.
accepted: There is some bread in the kitchen
There’s some bread in the kitchen
There is some bread in the kitchen.

days.titleUz: Böş vaqt, qiziqişlar va hafta oxiri rejalari
days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: böş vaqt va havas sözlari, “can / can’t” bilan qobiliyat, “am / is / are going to” bilan yakşanba rejalari.

sections.titleUz: Yangi sözlar: böş vaqt va qiziqişlar
Grammatika: can / can’t va going to
Öqiş: “Böş vaqtim va dam oliş kunim”

exercises.instructionUz: Test: “kinoteatr” sözining inglizçasini belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: cinema — kinoteatr.
exercises.question: Which word means "kinoteatr"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: töğri şaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: “can”dan keyin fe’l öz şaklida — sing.
exercises.question: My sister can ___ three English songs.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: reja haqidagi töğri gapni belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: “he” bilan is going to işlatiladi.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is going to swim on Sunday.
He going to swim on Sunday.
He goes to swim on Sunday.
He is going swim on Sunday.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: böş joylarni töldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: Iloj bor — can, yöq — can’t; reja — am going to.
exercises.text: I ___ dance, but I ___ swim. On Sunday I ___ going to ride a bike.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 6-kun öqiş matnini eslab, baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda boğda basketbol maydoni bor deyilgan, suziş havzasi aytilmagan.
exercises.statement: There is a basketball court in the park.
exercises.evidence: There is a small lake in the park, and there is a court for basketball next to it.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 6-kun tinglaş matniga asoslanib baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Farrukh filmni amakivaççasi (cousin — amaki yoki toqaning farzandi) bilan körmoqçi.
exercises.statement: Farrukh is going to watch a film with his cousin on Sunday.
exercises.evidence: On Sunday I am going to watch a film with my cousin. Do you want to come?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sözlarni töğri tartibda qöying.
exercises.explanationUz: Töğri gap: Are you going to play basketball this weekend?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni inglizçaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Men ertaga kinoteatrga bormoqçiman” = I am going to the cinema ...
accepted: I am going to the cinema tomorrow
I’m going to the cinema tomorrow
I want to go to the cinema tomorrow
I’d like to go to the cinema tomorrow

days.titleUz: Sayohat, yöl söraş va hafta yakuniy takrori
days.goalUz: Işlatiladi: transport va sayohat sözlari, yöl söraş (How do I get to ...?, Turn left), “was / were” bilan keçagi joylar — keyin butun hafta takrori testi.

sections.titleUz: Yangi sözlar: transport, bekat va yöl belgilari
Grammatika: yöl söraş va was / were
Gapiriş: transport, yöl körsatiş, keçagi joylar

exercises.instructionUz: Test: töğri fe’l şaklini belgilang (1-kun: to be).
exercises.explanationUz: “She” — uçinçi şaxs yagona, şuning uçun is.
exercises.question: She ___ a teacher and I ___ her student.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: oila a’zosi sözini tanlang (2-kun: family).
exercises.explanationUz: Amaki yoki toqaning qizi/öğli ingliz tilida “cousin” deyiladi.
exercises.question: My uncle’s daughter is my ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: kunlik tartib haqidagi gaplarni töldiring (3-kun: present simple).
exercises.explanationUz: I bilan get / have işlatiladi — present simple, şaxsga -s qöşilmaydi.
exercises.text: Every morning I ___ up at half past six. Then I ___ breakfast with my family at seven o’clock.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: joy va “there is/are” (4-kun).
exercises.explanationUz: “two buses” köplik — There are; bekat esa binoning YONIDA — next to.
exercises.question: ___ two buses at the stop, and the stop is ___ our building.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni özbekçaga tarjima qiling (5-kun: some / any).
exercises.explanationUz: He isn’t thirsty — “u çanqagan emas”; inkor gapda any keladi — “suv ham xohlamaydi”.
exercises.source: He isn’t thirsty, and he doesn’t want any water.
accepted: U çanqagan emas va u heç qanday suv xohlamaydi
U çanqagan emas, unga suv kerak emas
U çanqoq emas va suv xohlamaydi
U çanqagan emas va u suv ham xohlamaydi
U çanqoq emas, unga suv ham kerak emas

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sözlarni töğri qöyib, reja haqidagi gap tuzing (6-kun: going to).
exercises.explanationUz: Töğri gap: We are going to visit the museum next Sunday.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 7-kun öqiş matniga asoslanib baho bering (was / were).
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda “on Sunday morning we were in Samarkand” deyilgan, şuning uçun fikr töğri.
exercises.statement: The family was in Samarkand on Sunday morning.
exercises.evidence: We were on a big train for three hours, and on Sunday morning we were in Samarkand.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: yöl körsatiş gapini inglizçaga tarjima qiling (7-kun).
exercises.explanationUz: Çapga buriling = Turn left; töğri boring = go straight ahead.
accepted: Turn left and go straight ahead
Turn left and go straight
Turn left and go straight ahead.

vocab.explanationEn: You say this when you meet someone.
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, my name is Samir.

vocab.explanationEn: You say this when you leave.
vocab.exampleEn: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

vocab.explanationEn: A word for a person, a city or a thing.
vocab.exampleEn: What is your name?

vocab.explanationEn: The start of the day, before twelve o’clock.
vocab.exampleEn: Good morning! I am late.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where students have lessons.
vocab.exampleEn: Our classroom is big and clean.
vocab.exampleUz: Bizning sinf xonamiz katta va toza.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who studies at a school or a university.
vocab.exampleEn: I am a student at School Number Seven.

vocab.explanationEn: A person whose job is teaching people.
vocab.exampleEn: Our English teacher is very kind.
vocab.exampleUz: Bizning ingliz tili öqituvçimiz juda mehribon.

vocab.explanationEn: You read a book. It has many pages.
vocab.exampleEn: This book has twenty pages.

vocab.explanationEn: A tool for writing with ink.
vocab.exampleEn: Is this your pen or my pen?

vocab.explanationEn: A tool for writing. You can erase a pencil.
vocab.exampleEn: I have a new pencil and an eraser.
vocab.exampleUz: Menda yangi qalam va öçirğiç bor.

vocab.explanationEn: A table for one student at school.
vocab.exampleEn: There are twenty desks in our classroom.

vocab.explanationEn: A word like one, two, ten or twenty.
vocab.exampleEn: My number is seven and my age is eleven.
vocab.exampleUz: Mening raqamim yetti, yoşim ön bir.

vocab.explanationEn: The people you live with: parents, brothers and sisters.
vocab.exampleEn: My family has five people.

vocab.explanationEn: Your mother and your father together.
vocab.exampleEn: My parents are teachers.

vocab.explanationEn: A girl with the same mother and father as you.
vocab.exampleEn: My sister Nilufar is fifteen.

vocab.explanationEn: A boy with the same mother and father as you.
vocab.exampleEn: My brother Sanjar is eight years old.

vocab.explanationEn: The mother of your mother or your father.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother is seventy years old.

vocab.explanationEn: The father of your mother or your father.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather has a small garden.

vocab.explanationEn: The sister of your mother or your father.
vocab.exampleEn: My aunt has two sons.

vocab.explanationEn: The son or daughter of your aunt or uncle.
vocab.exampleEn: My cousin is eleven and he is tall.
vocab.exampleUz: Amakivaççam ön bir yoşda, u baland böyli.

vocab.explanationEn: Not short. Your father can be tall.
vocab.exampleEn: My father is tall and kind.

vocab.explanationEn: Not tall. Also: not long, like a short book.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother is short and quiet.
vocab.exampleUz: Bibim böyiga past va xulqi tinç.

vocab.explanationEn: Not old. A young person is fourteen, for example.
vocab.exampleEn: The students in my class are young.

vocab.explanationEn: The soft thing that grows on your head.
vocab.exampleEn: She has long black hair.

vocab.explanationEn: To stop sleeping in the morning.
vocab.exampleEn: I wake up at six thirty.

vocab.explanationEn: To leave your bed after you wake up.
vocab.exampleEn: I get up fast and put on my uniform.

vocab.explanationEn: The first food of your day, in the morning.
vocab.exampleEn: I have breakfast with my family.

vocab.explanationEn: You do this to your teeth every morning.
vocab.exampleEn: I brush my teeth every morning.

vocab.explanationEn: Special clothes that all students in a school wear.
vocab.exampleEn: My school uniform is blue and white.
vocab.exampleUz: Mening maktab formam kök va oq.

vocab.explanationEn: The food you eat in the middle of the day.
vocab.exampleEn: We have lunch at twelve o’clock.

vocab.explanationEn: A thing you study at school, like maths or English.
vocab.exampleEn: My favourite subject is English.

vocab.explanationEn: School work that the teacher gives you for home.
vocab.exampleEn: I do my homework at half past four.
vocab.exampleUz: Uy vazifamni soat tört yarimda qilaman.

vocab.explanationEn: Most of the time, but not always.
vocab.exampleEn: I usually drink tea for breakfast.

vocab.explanationEn: Saturday and Sunday. You do not go to school.
vocab.exampleEn: On the weekend I get up late.

vocab.explanationEn: We say it for a full hour: at six o’clock.
vocab.exampleEn: School starts at eight o’clock.

vocab.explanationEn: Before the usual time. Early is the opposite of late.
vocab.exampleEn: I go to bed early on Sunday.

vocab.explanationEn: A building where a family lives.
vocab.exampleEn: Our house is small but warm.

vocab.explanationEn: A part of a house with walls and a door.
vocab.exampleEn: There are five rooms in our flat.

vocab.explanationEn: The room where people cook food.
vocab.exampleEn: My mother cooks dinner in the kitchen.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where you sleep.
vocab.exampleEn: My bedroom is small and clean.
vocab.exampleUz: Mening yotiş xonam kiçik va toza.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where you wash and take a bath.
vocab.exampleEn: The bathroom is next to the kitchen.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where a family sits together in the evening.
vocab.exampleEn: The TV is in the living room.

vocab.explanationEn: A part of a wall with glass. You look outside through it.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two windows in the kitchen.

vocab.explanationEn: You put things on it and eat at it.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two books on the table.

vocab.explanationEn: You sit on it.
vocab.exampleEn: The chair is next to the table.

vocab.explanationEn: You sleep on it at night.
vocab.exampleEn: My bed is soft and clean.

vocab.explanationEn: Below something, with the thing over it.
vocab.exampleEn: The cat sleeps under the chair.

vocab.explanationEn: At the side of something, very near it.
vocab.exampleEn: The lamp is next to the window.

vocab.explanationEn: Food made from flour. You cannot count it.
vocab.exampleEn: There is some bread on the table.

vocab.explanationEn: Small white grains you cook and eat.
vocab.exampleEn: We sometimes have rice and meat for lunch.
vocab.exampleUz: Tuşlikda ba’zan guruç va göşt eymiz.

vocab.explanationEn: You can count eggs: one egg, two eggs.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two eggs in the fridge.

vocab.explanationEn: A round fruit. You can count apples.
vocab.exampleEn: I eat an apple every day.

vocab.explanationEn: A white food made from milk. It is uncountable.
vocab.exampleEn: There isn’t any cheese at home.

vocab.explanationEn: A white drink from a cow. You cannot count it.
vocab.exampleEn: I drink warm milk at night.

vocab.explanationEn: You drink it every day. It is uncountable.
vocab.exampleEn: Can I have some water, please?

vocab.explanationEn: Food that comes from an animal.
vocab.exampleEn: My uncle does not eat any meat.

vocab.explanationEn: You put food in your mouth.
vocab.exampleEn: I eat soup for dinner.

vocab.explanationEn: You take water or tea into your mouth.

grammar.titleUz: To be fe’li: am / is / are
grammar.titleEn: The verb to be: am / is / are
explanationUz: Ingliz tilida “men talabaman”, “u öqituvçi”, “biz döstmiz” deganda “to be” fe’li işlatiladi. Özbek tilida bunday gapda fe’l bölmaydi, ingliz tilida esa fe’l albatta kerak: I am a student, She is a teacher. Fe’lsiz gap ingliz tilida xato hisoblanadi.

To be fe’li şaxsga qarab uç şaklga ega: I bilan am işlatiladi; he, she, it va yagona narsa bilan is; we, you, they va köplikdagi narsalar bilan are. Eslab qoliş uçun uçta qatorni takrorlang: I am — you are — he is / she is / it is — we are — they are.

Inkor gapda to be fe’lidan keyin not qöyiladi: I am not late. She is not (isn’t) a teacher. They are not (aren’t) in the classroom. Söroq gapda esa to be fe’li ega oldinga çiqadi: Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I am not. Is her name Aziza? — Yes, it is.

Sözlaşuvda qisqartmalar juda köp işlatiladi: I’m, she’s, he’s, they’re, we’re. Inkorda esa isn’t, aren’t, ‘m not şakllari uçraydi. Yozma testlarda qisqartma va töliq şakl ikkalasi ham töğri javobdir, lekin bitta gapda fe’lni ikki marta qaytariş xato: “I am a student, am a teacher” deb yozilmaydi.

grammar.titleUz: Egalik: ’s, my / your va have got
grammar.titleEn: Possessives: ’s, my / your, and have got
explanationUz: Narsa kimniki ekanini aytiş uçun ingliz tilida ismga ’s qöşiladi: Bekzod’s book (Bekzodning kitobi), my sister’s bag (singilmning sumkasi). Agar egalardan bir neçta bölsa va ular bir narsaga tegişli bölsa, ’s oxirgi ismga qöyiladi: Aziz and Malika’s home. Egalik “of” bilan ham aytiladi, lekin A1 darajasida ’s eng tabiiy yöldir.

my, your, his, her, our, their sözlari “kimniki” degan savolga javob beradi va har doim ot oldida keladi: my book, your pen, his name, her hair, our class, their friends. Bu sözlar özi egalikni bildiradi, ularga ’s qöşilmaydi: “my book” (heç qaçon “my’s book” emas). Javobda otni takrorlamaslik ham mumkin: “Is this your pen?” — “Yes, it is my pen.”

Biror narsaga ega ekanlikni have got bilan aytkazamiz: I have got a bike. She has got two brothers. Uçinçi şaxs yagonada has işlatilişini unutmang. Inkor: I haven’t got a phone. She hasn’t got a bike. Söroq: Have you got a pen? Has he got a red bag? Qisqartmalar sözlaşuvda köp: I’ve got, she’s got, he hasn’t got.

Odamni tasvirlaşda ham have got işlatiladi: He has got short black hair. She has got blue eyes. Sifatlar ot oldida keladi va köplikda özgarmaydi: two tall boys (tall söziga -lar qöşilmaydi). Kasb, yoş va kayfiyat esa to be fe’li bilan aytiladi: She is a teacher. He is eight. Bu ikki tuzilmani aralaştirmang: egalik — have got, sifat, kasb va yoş — to be.

grammar.titleEn: Present Simple and talking about time
explanationUz: Har kuni takrorlanadigan işlarimizni Present Simple zamoni bilan aytamiz: I get up at six. She goes to school at eight. Bu zamon “men odatda şunday qilaman” degan ma’noni beradi, şuning uçun “every day”, “usually”, “never”, “on Monday” kabi sözlar köp işlatiladi.

Ega uçinçi şaxs yagona bölsa (he, she, it, my mother, Bekzod), fe’lga -s yoki -es qöşiladi: he plays, she goes, he watches, she has. “have” → “has”, “go” → “goes”, “do” → “does” şakllarini alohida eslab qoliş kerak. Boşqa şaxslarda fe’l özgarmaydi: I play, you play, we play, they play.

Inkor va söroq gaplarda yordamçi fe’l do / does keladi va asosiy fe’l -siz qoladi: I do not (don’t) watch TV. He does not (doesn’t) get up late. Do you go to school by bus? Does she like English? “He doesn’t goes” deb ikki marta -s qöyilmaydi.

Vaqt bildirişda prepozitsiyalarni çalkaştirmang: soat bilan — at (at eight o’clock, at half past six); hafta kuni bilan — on (on Monday, on Friday); kunduz qismlari bilan — in (in the morning, in the evening). “half past six” — oltidan yarim ötgan, 6:30; “a quarter past seven” — 7:15; “a quarter to nine” — sakkizdan çorak qoldi, 8:45. Kunlar katta harf bilan yoziladi: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

grammar.titleUz: There is / there are va joy bildiruvçi predloglar
grammar.titleEn: There is / there are and prepositions of place
explanationUz: Uyda yoki xonada biror narsa borligini aytiş uçun ingliz tilida “there is” va “there are” işlatiladi. Bitta narsa uçun there is, ikki yoki undan köp narsa uçun there are qöllanadi. Özbekçadagi “bor” sözi bu yerda fe’l şakliga qarab ikki xil böladi: There is a bed. / There are two beds.

There is köpinça qisqartirilib “there’s” deyiladi: There’s a lamp in my room. Inkor şakli — there is not (there isn’t) va there are not (there aren’t): There isn’t a TV in my room. There aren’t any chairs in the kitchen.

Narsa qayerda turişini bildiriş uçun in, on, under, next to predloglari işlatiladi. “in” — içida: in the kitchen, in the box. “on” — ustida: on the table, on the wall. “under” — ostida: under the bed. “next to” — yonida: next to the door.

Bu gap tartibi özbekçadan farq qiladi. Özbekçada joy sözi gapning oxirida keladi (“Kitob stol ustida”), ingliz tilida esa predlog töğridan-töğri fe’ldan (is / are) keyin keladi: The book is on the table. Şuning uçun “The book is” deb qoldirmang, joy albatta aytiladi.

Söroq quriş uçun is yoki are egadan oldinga çiqadi: Is there a bathroom in your flat? Are there windows in the kitchen? Qisqa javoblar: Yes, there is. / No, there isn’t. / Yes, there are. / No, there aren’t.

formula.form: There is + a / an + bitta narsa
formula.noteUz: Bitta narsa uçun: There is a sofa in the living room.
Ikki yoki undan köp: There are four chairs in the kitchen.

formula.form: There is not (isn’t) / There are not (aren’t)
formula.noteUz: Inkor uçun not qöşiladi: There isn’t a lamp here.
Söroqda is/are oldinga çiqadi.

formula.form: narsa + is / are + (in | on | under | next to) + joy
formula.noteUz: The cat is under the table.

grammar.titleUz: Some / any, sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan ismlar, like + -ing
grammar.titleEn: Some / any, countable and uncountable nouns, like + -ing
explanationUz: Ovqat va içimliklar haqida gapirganda “biroz / bir neça” ma’nosida some işlatiladi. Some tasdiq gaplarda keladi va ham sanaladigan, ham sanalmaydigan ism bilan işlaydi: There is some bread on the table. There are some eggs in the fridge.

Inkor va söroq gaplarda esa any işlatiladi: There isn’t any milk. Are there any apples? Any ham sanaladigan köplik, ham sanalmaydigan ism bilan keladi. Ruxsat söraş yoki taklif qilişda esa some işlatiladi: Can I have some water? Would you like some tea?

Ingliz tilida ismlar ikki turga bölinadi. Sanaladigan ismlar bitta va köplik şaklga ega: an apple — two apples, an egg — three eggs. Ulardan oldin a/an qöyiladi va köplikda -s qöşiladi. Sanalmaydigan ismlar (bread, rice, water, milk, cheese, meat) heç qaçon -s olamaydi va ular bilan “is” işlatiladi: The rice is hot. There is some rice in the box.

Miqdor söraşda how many sanaladigan köplik bilan, how much esa sanalmaydigan ism bilan keladi: How many eggs do we need? How much water do you drink? Sanalmaydigan ism miqdori idiş orqali aytiladi: a glass of water, a cup of tea, a kilo of rice.

Biror narsani yoqtirişni aytişda like va enjoy’den keyin fe’l -ing şaklida keladi: I like cooking. My parents enjoy eating together. Inkor şakl — like’ni don’t / doesn’t bilan: I don’t like soup. She doesn’t like cooking fish.

grammar.titleUz: Can / can’t (qila oliş, qöl keliş) va “going to” bilan reja
grammar.titleEn: Can / can’t for ability and “going to” for plans
explanationUz: Biror işni bila oliş yoki qila olişni aytiş uçun “can” işlatiladi. “Can”dan keyin fe’l doim öz şaklida keladi: heç qanday -s, -ing yoki “to” qöşilmaydi. I can swim. She can play the guitar. He can ride a bike.

Qila olmaslikni “can’t” (can not) bilan aytamiz: I can’t swim. My brother can’t dance. Söroqda “can” egadan oldin çiqadi: Can you dance? Can your sister sing? Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I can. / No, I can’t.
“Can”dan keyingi fe’l şaxsga qarab özgarmasligini esda saqlang: “She cans”, “He can plays” deyilmaydi. Töğri: She can sing, he can sing. Bu qoida boşqa fe’llardan farq qiladi.

Kelasi hafta yoki yakşanba uçun rejangiz borligini aytişda “be + going to” işlatiladi: I am going to watch a film. We are going to play football in the park. Bu yerda “am / is / are” şaxsga mos tanlanadi: I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are.

Reja haqidagi söroqda “am / is / are” egadan oldinga çiqadi: What are you going to do on Saturday? Where is she going to play? Inkor uçun not qöşiladi: I am not going to stay at home. Rejalar köpinça aniq vaqt bilan keladi: on Saturday, at nine o’clock, this weekend.

grammar.titleEn: Asking for directions and was / were
explanationUz: Biror joyga qanday borişni söraş uçun “Excuse me, how do I get to ...?” deyiladi. Javobda yöl körsatiş gaplari işlatiladi: “Go straight ahead” — töğri boring; “Turn left” — çapga buriling; “Turn right” — öngga buriling. Joy yaqin yoki uzoq ekanini “It is near” va “It is far” bilan aytamiz.

Yöl körsatişda 4-kundagi joy predloglari yana kerak böladi: “The station is next to the gate”, “The bus stop is in front of the shop”, “The crossing is under the bridge”. Şuning uçun yöl söraş mavzusi oldingi kunlar bilan bevosita boğlangan.

Keçagi yoki oldingi biror joyda bölganimizni aytiş uçun “to be” fe’lining ötgan zamoni — was va were — işlatiladi. “I was, he was, she was, it was”; “we were, you were, they were”. Özbekçadagi “... edim / ... edik” şu ikki şaklga töğri keladi: I was at home. We were at the station.

Inkor şakli: was not (wasn’t) va were not (weren’t): I wasn’t at the airport. They weren’t in the train. Söroqda was / were egadan oldinga çiqadi: Where were you yesterday? Was the museum interesting? Qisqa javob: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t.

“Was / were” faqat bitta holat yoki joy haqida işlatiladi, harakat fe’llari bilan emas. A1 darajasida “I was happy”, “We were in Samarkand” kabi gaplar yetarli. Harakatni esa “We went ...” yoki “We were on a train” kabi sodda iboralar bilan ifodalaymiz.

paragraphs: My name is Dilnoza and I am thirteen years old. I live in Tashkent with my family. My family is not big: there are five people in it — my mother, my father, my little brother, my grandmother and me.

My mother's name is Malika. She is thirty-two and she is a teacher. She is tall and she has got long black hair. My father's name is Rustam. He is thirty-five. He is short, he is quiet, and he has got a blue bike.

My little brother is Sanjar. He is eight years old and he has got a big red bag. My grandmother lives with us. Her hair is short and grey and she is very kind. Our home is small, but our family is warm. I love my family.

reading.title: My Day, Hour by Hour
paragraphs: My name is Aziza and I am twelve years old. I wake up at half past six every morning. First I brush my teeth and wash my face. Then I have breakfast with my family. I usually drink hot tea and eat bread with cheese.

I put on my school uniform and walk to school. School starts at eight o’clock and I am never late. My favourite subject is English. I also like maths and art. We have lunch at twelve o’clock at school, and school finishes at two o’clock. I come home with my friend Nilufar.

In the afternoon I do my homework. It is often difficult, but I like it. At half past five I play tennis with my brother or I draw a picture. We have dinner together at half past eight. I go to bed at nine o’clock and sleep nine hours. On Saturday and Sunday I do not get up early — I sleep until ten!

paragraphs: I live in a flat in Tashkent with my family. My flat is not big, but it is warm and clean. There are five rooms: a living room, two bedrooms, a kitchen and a bathroom. The kitchen is next to the bathroom.
My favourite room is my bedroom. There is a bed, a small table and a lamp in my bedroom. My books are on the table, and my school bag is under the chair. A picture of my family is on the wall.

In the living room there is a soft sofa and a TV. In the evening my family sits there together. My little brother often plays under the table. There are no computers in our rooms, because my mother says: “Games are not good for you.”

reading.title: Food for the Weekend
paragraphs: On Saturday morning I go to the market near my house with my mother. We need some food for the weekend. We buy two kilos of rice, some meat and ten eggs. The market is big and there are a lot of people there.

At home we put the food on the table. There isn’t any milk in the fridge, so my father goes to the small shop near our building. I like cooking, so I make soup and a salad. Are there any apples in the bag? Yes, there are five apples!

In the evening my family eats together at the big table. My little sister drinks tea with sugar, but she doesn’t like soup. My parents enjoy eating with our neighbours, so we invite them on Sunday. Food is always better with friends.

paragraphs: My name is Sardor and I am thirteen. I like my free time because I can do the things I love. I can play football very well, and I can ride a bike for two hours. My sister can dance, but she can’t swim.

This weekend is special. On Saturday Farrukh and I are going to watch a film at the cinema in the city. On Sunday I am not going to stay at home, because my father and I are going to ride bikes in the hills. I love my weekends.

paragraphs: Tashkent is a big city. There are many buses and a metro here, and there is a long bridge over the river. I go to school by bus every day, because the bus stop is next to our building and a ticket is cheap.

Last weekend was different. On Saturday my family and I were at the railway station in Tashkent. We were on a big train for three hours, and on Sunday morning we were in Samarkand. My little sister was very happy, because she saw a big square and very old buildings.

In the city, I asked a man, “Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?” He said, “Go straight ahead and turn left at the crossing. The museum is next to the blue gate.” We were at the museum in five minutes. The museum was old and very interesting.

writing.promptEn: Write a short email to your new English class. Say your name, your age, your school and the things you have in your bag.
writing.instructionUz: Yangi ingliz tili sinfingizga qisqa xat yozing. Özingizni taniştiring: ismingiz, yoşingiz, maktabingiz va sumkangizda narsalar borligini ayting. To be fe’lini (am / is / are) kamida uç marta işlatişga harakat qiling.
checklistUz: Xat boşlanişi va oxiri bor (Hello ... / Goodbye ...).
Ismingiz va yoşingiz töğri yozilgan.
To be fe’li kamida uç marta işlatilgan.
Sumkangizdagi ikkita buyum nomlangan.
Gaplar katta harf bilan boşlanib, nuqta bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Taniştiriş uçun “My name is ...” iborasi albatta kerak.
Yoş, maktab va his-tuyğu “I am ...” bilan aytiladi.
Sinf buyumlari mavzusini oçiş uçun sumkadagi narsalar sanaladi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hello! My name is Aziza. I am twelve years old and I am a student at School Number Five. My classroom is big. I have two books, a pen and a pencil in my bag. I am happy to meet you. Thank you! Goodbye, Aziza.

writing.instructionUz: Döstingizga inglizça qisqa xabar yozing: oilangizda neçta kişi borligini ayting, bitta oila a’zosini tavsiflang (yoşi, soçi, böyi) va uning nimaga ega ekanligini have got bilan körsating.
checklistUz: Oiladagi kişilar soni angliyça son bilan yozilgan.
Bitta kişining yoşi va taşqi körinişi bor.
have got / has got kamida bitta marta işlatilgan.
Egalik şakli ('s yoki my/your) kamida bitta marta işlatilgan.
Xabar salom bilan boşlanib, döstona tamomlangan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Mavzuga kiriş uçun “My family has ...” gap kerak.
Egalik va tavsifda has / have got şakli işlatilişi talab qilinadi.
Tavsif obyekti aniq bölişi uçun yaqin qarindoş tanlanadi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Aziza! My family has five people: my mother, my father, my little brother, my grandmother and me. My mother’s name is Malika. She is thirty-two and she is tall. She has got long black hair. My father has got a blue bike. I love my family! See you at school, Dilnoza.

writing.promptEn: Write a paragraph about your day. Say what time you wake up, get up and go to school. Say what you do in the afternoon and what time you go to bed.

checklistUz: Kamida uçta vaqt körsatilgan (uyoniş, maktab, uxlaş).
Present Simple fe’llari töğri işlatilgan (I go, I do, I have).
at + soat qoidasi saqlangan.
Kunduzdan keyingi bir faoliyat aytilgan.
Paragraf bitta butun matn bölib, nuqtalar qöyilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Kunlik tartibni boşlaş uçun “I wake up at ...” gap kerak.
Kunni tugatiş uçun “I go to bed at ...” gapini yoziş kerak.
Kun davomiy körsatilsin deb kunduzgi faoliyat sanaladi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: I wake up at half past six and I get up fast. I brush my teeth and I have breakfast at seven o’clock. I go to school at eight o’clock. School finishes at two o’clock and I come home. In the afternoon I do my homework and I play tennis with my brother. I go to bed at nine o’clock and I sleep nine hours.

Sevimli xona tanlanib, undagi kamida uç narsa sanalgan.
Kamida uç xil joy predlogi işlatilgan (in / on / under / next to).
Kamida bitta inkor gap bor (there isn’t / there aren’t).
Gaplar katta harf bilan boşlanib, nuqta bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Bitta narsa borligini aytiş uçun “There is ...” kerak.
Köp narsa borligini aytiş uçun “There are ...” kerak.
Narsa joyini körsatiş uçun predloglar (masalan “under”) albatta kerak.

writing.modelAnswerEn: My home is a flat in Tashkent. There are four rooms: a living room, two bedrooms and a kitchen. My favourite room is my bedroom. There is a bed, a desk and a small lamp in it. My books are on the desk and my shoes are under the bed. There isn’t a TV in my room. I like my flat because it is quiet and clean.

writing.promptEn: Write a message to a friend. Tell them what food you have at home, what you don’t have, and what you like cooking.

Kamida bitta inkor yoki söroq gapda “any” işlatilgan.
“I like ...ing” iborasi bilan bir faoliyat aytilgan.
Kamida beş ta ovqat yoki içimlik sözi işlatilgan.
Xabar salom bilan boşlanib, ism bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Bor narsani aytiş uçun “some” kerak: There is some bread.
Yöq narsani aytiş uçun inkor gapda “any” kerak: There isn’t any milk.
Yoqtirgan faoliyat “like + -ing” bilan yoziladi: I like cooking.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Dilnoza! On Saturday I want to cook lunch at my home. There is some rice and there are six eggs in the fridge. There is also some bread and there are five apples in the bag. There isn’t any cheese and there aren’t any tomatoes. I like cooking rice with meat, and my sister likes making salad. Can you come at one o’clock? We can eat together. Your friend, Bekzod.

writing.promptEn: Write an email to your friend about your weekend. What are you going to do on Saturday and Sunday, and what can you do well?

Kamida ikkita “am / is / are going to” bilan reja aytilgan.
Kamida bitta “can” va bitta “can’t” işlatilgan.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Bekzod! This weekend is very busy for me. On Saturday I am going to play football with my friends in the park. We are going to play from nine to eleven. I can play football well, but I can’t play basketball. I can bring water and apples. Do you want to come? On Sunday I am going to ride a bike with my father in the hills. In the evening my cousin is going to play the guitar at our home. Write to me soon! Your friend, Sardor.

writing.promptEn: Write a message to a friend about a trip. Where were you, how did you travel, and how do you get there?
writing.instructionUz: Döstingizga inglizça xabar yozing. Qayerda bölganingizni “I was ... / We were ...” bilan ayting, qanday transportda borganningizni körsating va öşa yerga qanday boriş yölini “Go straight ahead ... Turn left / right ...” bilan tuşuntiring. Kamida bitta rejangizni “I am going to ...” bilan qöşib yozing.
checklistUz: Xabarda kamida ikkita “was / were” bilan gap bor.
Transport turi aytilgan (by bus, by train, by metro).
Yöl körsatiş iborasi qöllanilgan (Go straight ahead / Turn left / Turn right).
Biror joyning yaqin yoki uzoq ekanini aytilgan (near / far).
Xabar salom bilan boşlanib, ism bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Ötgan kun qayerda bölganingizni “I was / it was” bilan aytiladi.
Sayohat mavzusida transport joyi (station) albatta kerak.
Yöl körsatiş uçun “Go straight ahead” iborasi talab qilinadi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Nilufar! Last weekend was great. On Saturday my family and I were at the railway station in Tashkent. We went to Samarkand by train, and the station was big and clean. On Sunday we wanted to see the museum. It was not far from the station. A man helped us: “Go straight ahead and turn left at the crossing. The museum is next to the blue gate.” The museum was old and very interesting. Next month I am going to visit Samarkand again. Write to me soon! Your friend, Sardor.

speaking.questionEn: In your home, where is the TV and where do you do your homework?

What was in that place?

Hi, Sardor! Yes, I am. What are you doing?

That sounds great! What time do we meet?
Let's meet at nine o'clock, at the main gate of the park.
OK. I'm bringing fruit and water. Can your brother come too?
Yes, he can. He is making a cake for everyone on Friday evening.
Perfect! What's the weather like on Friday? Is it going to rain?
The radio says it will be sunny all weekend, so we're lucky.
Wonderful. See you on Saturday then. Goodbye, Sardor!
Bye, Dilnoza! See you at nine.

writingTask.promptEn: Write an email to your English teacher. Tell her: (1) what you did last weekend, (2) what you are doing now, (3) when you can have the next lesson.
